references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the synagogue ruler (Jairus) who came to Jesus because his daughter was dead, and Jesus accompanying him.

Mark's parallel account where some come from the synagogue ruler's house saying that the daughter is dead and that he should not trouble the teacher any longer. Jesus encourages Jairus not to be afraid but only to believe.
The preceding context in Luke where Jairus, a synagogue ruler, comes to Jesus and asks him to come to his house because his only daughter was at the point of death.
Continuation of the account where Jesus tells Jairus not to fear but only to believe, and then goes in and raises the girl from the dead.
A similar situation where someone is sent with a message while Jesus is on the way – an officer sends friends to say that Jesus does not need to come all the way to his house.

Martha says to Jesus that her brother Lazarus would not have died if Jesus had been there, but that she knows God will give him whatever he asks – a similar theme that it seems too late, yet Jesus has power over death.
Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead even though it seems too late – parallel to Jesus showing his power over death despite the message that the girl was already dead.
